title: Expose WebGL loss and make short landscape HUD preserve centered gestures

scope.subject: Small read-only presentation layer over the existing renderer lifecycle and short-landscape responsive HUD with real browser regressions.

research_summary: Round 2 independently reproduced two product concerns on the deployed artifact: native context loss is invisible even though restoration works, and the fixed width HUD consumes one finger of a standard landscape centered pinch. Browser-native lifecycle, CSS sizing and existing Portfolio are sufficient. No engine, scheduling, world state, touch algorithm or CI change.

sources.finding: Existing renderer is the owner of the lost/active/released attribute; no change to its lifecycle or callback required.
A filtered browser observer can mirror precisely the existing data attribute at the UI boundary with no timer, canvas listeners or second renderer owner.
Use a pre-existing status live region with polite implicit announcement for transient rendering loss.
Use orientation and viewport height to adapt HUD layout without treating a device class as a gesture capability.
Existing HUD already handles the current locale and link to the static Portfolio. Keep all controls and use the existing fallback route.

search_ladder.conclusion: Use the current universe and static portfolio; no full product replacement.
Reuse installed renderer lifecycle signals and React presentation.
Existing lifecycle authority and Portfolio already supply the loss state and fallback destination.
Use the ARIA status primitive and CSS media queries, plus real Chromium device input via existing Playwright.

candidates.name: Existing Three/R3F WebGL lifecycle
candidates.source: Existing installed capability or browser standard
candidates.reason: Reuse its exact lifecycle attribute rather than engine listeners.

candidates.name: Native WebGL restoration
candidates.source: Existing installed capability or browser standard
candidates.reason: The browser owns restoration; use the existing Portfolio route while 3D is unavailable.

candidates.name: React UI and standard CSS media query
candidates.source: Existing installed capability or browser standard
candidates.reason: Mirror one externally held UI flag using a filtered observer and effect cleanup; use compact CSS sizing for short landscape.

candidates.name: Playwright and real Chromium CDP input
candidates.source: Existing installed capability or browser standard
candidates.reason: Use genuine WebGL_lose_context and real Chromium touch input instead of synthetic React events.

decision.rationale: No duplication of the WebGL lifecycle or gesture authority. Preserve compact controls while moving the left overlay away from the centered gesture. Prove exact touch hit target and real loss/restore.
decision.fallback: Keep the current working browser recovery and explicit static Portfolio route; defer physical mobile Safari validation to a supported device.
